entries.title: Film Noir
entries.text:
Film Noir

Film noir lighting is a low-key, high-contrast setup: a hard key, often cut by a venetian gobo or a streetlamp cookie, leaves one cheek in true black while wet pavement returns silver. The camera sits at eye height on a 35mm or 50mm spherical lens, tungsten practicals as motivated sources, and blocking that isolates a figure in a doorway, an alley, or a pool of light.

Create this Film Noir

Narrative function

The shot withholds the room. A face is half a mask.

Guilt has to live in the sliver that remains, which is why voice-over can sit on this image without explaining the picture. Streets are wet so the night has a specular path back to the lens.

It is the wrong tool when the crime is colorful, fashionable, or futuristic. If the threat is a gelled primary, use Giallo.

If the night is neon and the year is now, use Neo-Noir. If the architecture itself is bent, use German Expressionism, not a wet street.

How it works

Key with a hard Fresnel or open-face through slats, 45 to 90 degrees off camera, fill killed so the ratio sits near 8:1. Wet-down the street so the same key returns as bounce.

Practicals (desk lamp, cafe sign, streetlamp) must match the direction even if they are not the exposure. Lens: 35mm for a street, 50mm for a face, moderate stop so walls fall off.

Camera locked or a short dolly, eye level or a touch below. Prompt the gobo, the unfilled cheek, the wet asphalt, and 1940s crime blocking.

When to use it

Use it when a character steps under a streetlamp and the shadow has to accuse them. Do not use it as a generic dark-crime grade on a color-saturated fashion interior.

Compared with similar shots

Film noir is silver, hard, and unfilled. Neo-noir keeps the guilty geometry but paints it with color practicals.

Tech noir adds future screens as keys. Giallo is the opposite palette: hyper-saturated primaries, not black-and-white pools.

German Expressionism distorts the set; noir usually keeps real streets and lets light do the distortion. Kit cousins: Low-Key Lighting, Gobo Lighting, Wet-Down, Chiaroscuro.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

Gobo LightingThe room writes on the person.

Wet-DownNight exteriors that must sparkle.

In film

The Third Man (wet Vienna, hard raking keys, a face in a doorway). Double Indemnity (venetian gobos, a confession in a dark living room).

The Big Combo (a fogged spotlight as the only map of a killing ground). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Lead with the treatment, then lock physics. Film-noir treatment of [Subject], hard venetian gobos, unfilled far cheek, wet-down street bounce, 50mm spherical, 1940s crime blocking.

Name who stands where and which practical is the motivated key. Do not replace the gobo, the ratio, and the wet pavement with mood adjectives.

Use in Image Generator

Film-noir treatment of [Subject], hard venetian gobos, wet streets, fedora shadows, moral night, 1940s crime grammar.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Neo-Noir or generic Low-Key Lighting: color neon rain, or a softly underexposed room with no hard edge. The tell is a filled shadow, dry pavement, and no slat texture on the wall.

Fix: kill the fill, add a venetian or tree cookie, wet the ground, and keep the palette silver.

Questions

What is Film Noir in film?

A 1940s crime look built from hard, unfilled keys, gobo texture, wet streets, and eye-level 35mm or 50mm blocking. The picture withholds information. Silver contrast does the work that color would do in later noir.

Film Noir vs Neo-Noir

Film noir is low-key silver with tungsten practicals and wet-down bounce. Neo-noir keeps the guilty geometry but keys with color: sodium, neon, and contemporary flesh. If you can name a gel hue as the mood, you have left classic noir.

When should I use Film Noir?

When a crime scene needs the room to refuse the face: a doorway, a slatted office, a wet alley. Skip it for fashion-horror color, future screens, or any beat that needs a readable, filled close-up.

entries.title: Neo-Noir
entries.text:
Neo-Noir

Neo-noir cinematography keeps noir's hard keys and isolated blocking but replaces silver night with color: sodium vapor, neon practicals, and tungsten that stain rain and skin. The camera still hunts faces in shadow, yet the palette is contemporary, often cyan signage against warm flesh, not black-and-white contrast alone.

Create this Neo-Noir

Narrative function

The city is still a trap, but the trap has a hue. Rain carries magenta and cyan.

A sodium streetlamp turns a raincoat mustard. The moral geometry (half a face, a wet street, a figure stranded in a pool of light) survives.

Only the stock is color. It is the wrong tool when you need period silver, future screens as the only keys, or candy primaries as threat.

Classic Film Noir has no neon to name. Tech Noir puts crime inside a digital city.

Vaporwave uses pink-cyan without guilt or investigation.

How it works

Keep a hard key 45 to 90 degrees off, but let practical color do the fill: neon in rain, sodium overhead, a tungsten interior leaking onto wet asphalt. Contrast stays high.

Skin may go teal-shadow, orange-highlight, or stay mixed on purpose. Lens: 35mm or 40mm anamorphic, or spherical 35mm, often at night with rain as the volume.

Camera: locked wides, slow tracking, occasional push-in on a face. Prompt color where classic noir was silver, name the neon practicals, and keep the rain.

When to use it

Use it when a present-day or period-color crime scene needs melancholy and rain, not a 1940s silver print. Do not use it as a teal-and-orange grade on a scene with no hard key and no guilty blocking.

Compared with similar shots

Neo-Noir is color noir: same isolation, new practicals. Film Noir is the silver original.

Tech Noir adds science-fiction production design and screens as sources. Teal and Orange is a grade, not a genre look; you can grade a comedy teal-orange and still have no noir blocking.

Neon Practicals is the lamp. Neo-noir is the lamp plus the crime geometry.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

Neon PracticalsThe city is the lighting department.

Teal and OrangeYou want contemporary studio punch. Use with taste.

In film

Chinatown (period color, hard sun and venetian interiors, investigation as a trap). Blade Runner (rain, smoke, neon as key, still a detective picture).

Drive (night exteriors, pink-cyan practicals, locked-off melancholy). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Neo-noir look on [Subject], color where classic noir was silver, neon practicals, rain, contemporary crime blocking, hard key, unfilled far cheek. Name the hue of the signage and whether the camera is locked or tracking.

Do not write only teal and orange.

Use in Image Generator

Neo-noir look on [Subject], color where classic noir was silver, neon practicals, rain, contemporary crime melancholy.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Film Noir (you asked for color and got a black-and-white fedora) or a Teal and Orange grade with no key. The tell is a filled, even night or a palette with no motivated practical.

Fix: add a named neon or sodium source, keep the hard ratio, and wet the ground.

Questions

What is Neo-Noir in film?

Noir themes and blocking restaged after color: hard keys, rain, isolation, and crime, lit by sodium, neon, and tungsten instead of silver nitrate night.

Neo-Noir vs Film Noir

Film noir withholds with black-and-white contrast and tungsten gobos. Neo-noir withholds with color practicals. Same guilty geometry, different stock. If the frame has no hue you can name, it is not neo-noir.

When should I use Neo-Noir?

When a color crime scene needs rain, neon, and a face half in shadow. Skip it for 1940s silver, for future-corporate screens (Tech Noir), or for pastel mall nostalgia (Vaporwave).

How do I prompt Neo-Noir for AI image or video?

Write: Neo-noir look on [Subject], color where classic noir was silver, neon practicals, rain, hard key, unfilled cheek, contemporary crime blocking. Name cyan or magenta signage. Do not stop at a teal-orange slider.

entries.title: German Expressionism
entries.text:
German Expressionism

German Expressionism cinematography treats the set as a mind: forced-perspective corridors, painted shadows, and jagged hard light replace natural architecture. The camera is often locked and slightly dutch, so the actor walks a geometry that already looks illegal.

Create this German Expressionism

Narrative function

Psychology is built, not implied. A staircase leans.

A shadow is bigger than the body that casts it, and sometimes the shadow is paint. The face is lit like a mask because the room is already a diagnosis.

It is the wrong tool for a real wet street or a fashion interior. Noir keeps plausible cities and lets Hard Light do the violence.

Giallo bends color, not carpentry. If the walls are square and only the grade is moody, you do not have expressionism.

How it works

Build or paint impossible architecture: converging walls, oversized windows, stairs that refuse the horizon. Light with hard, unfilled sources so shadows are graphic edges, not soft falloff.

Dutch the camera a few degrees as a default, not a sting. Orthochromatic or high-contrast black-and-white, 35mm spherical, theatrical blocking, often locked-off.

Prompt painted shadows, impossible architecture, jagged light, and Caligari psychology as set.

When to use it

Use it when the location must be a mental state, not a real address. Do not use it as a dutch-angle garnish on a square contemporary room.

Compared with similar shots

German Expressionism distorts carpentry. Film Noir distorts with light on real streets.

Dutch Angle is one tilted horizon; expressionism is the whole set. Hard Light is the source quality.

Chiaroscuro is the ratio. You need the bent architecture, not only the contrast.

Dutch AngleThe world is off its axis. Do not use as decoration.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (painted shadows, canted town as a mind).

Metropolis (shafts, scale, and machine geometry as social diagram). Nosferatu (a body that is also a shadow on a wall).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

German expressionist treatment of [Subject], painted shadows, impossible architecture, jagged hard light, dutch horizon, theatrical blocking. Name which wall or stair is illegally angled.

Do not ask for a normal street with a moody grade.

Use in Image Generator

German expressionist treatment of [Subject], painted shadows, impossible architecture, jagged light, Caligari psychology as set.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Film Noir or a lone Dutch Angle: a wet alley, or a tilted camera in an ordinary room. The tell is square architecture with only contrast added.

Fix: cant the set or the perspective, paint or project graphic shadows, and lock the camera on that geometry.

Questions

What is German Expressionism in film?

A look in which distorted sets, painted or graphic shadows, hard unfilled light, and stylized blocking make the location a psychological diagram rather than a real street.

German Expressionism vs Film Noir

Noir keeps plausible cities and cuts them with gobos. Expressionism rebuilds the city as a bent mind. Both love hard light. Only one makes the staircase illegal.

When should I use German Expressionism?

When a character's inner state has to be walked through as architecture. Skip it for crime on real wet streets, for gelled fashion-horror, or for a dutch angle with nothing else changed.

How do I prompt German Expressionism for AI image or video?

Write: German expressionist treatment of [Subject], painted shadows, impossible architecture, jagged hard light, dutch horizon. Specify the illegal wall or stair. Do not prompt a normal room plus contrast.

entries.title: Giallo
entries.text:
Giallo

Giallo cinematography is Italian thriller grammar: hyper-saturated primaries from gelled windows and glass, fashion interiors, and a camera that often zooms rather than dollies toward threat. Beauty lighting sits on the victim. The violence is styled, not silver.

Create this Giallo

Narrative function

Horror here is also wardrobe. A cobalt window, a red hallway, black leather in the foreground.

The frame is chic until the glove enters. Subjective threat is a color, a zoom, and a Dutch Angle, not a wet black alley.

It is the wrong tool for low-key crime or for density-as-ornament. Film Noir withholds with black.

Maximalism fills every zone with pattern for pleasure. Giallo uses primaries as a weapon inside relatively designed, often sparse, interiors.

How it works

Gel the keys: red, green, cobalt through windows or colored glass, so the palette is primary, not pastel. Keep contrast high but chroma higher.

35 Techniscope wides for interiors. Dutch a few degrees on the kill or the stare.

Foreground a black glove, a blade, or a fashion object. Prompt hyper-saturated primaries, implied black leather, Argento color crime, and beauty as the lighting on the face, not a slogan.

When to use it

Use it when a stylish interior has to turn hostile through color, a zoom, and a gloved hand. Do not use it as generic saturated horror or as noir with a red grade.

Compared with similar shots

Giallo is gelled primaries and fashion-threat. Film Noir is unfilled silver.

Hyper-Saturation is a grade; giallo is that grade plus zoom, dutch, and leather-glove blocking. Maximalism packs ornament; giallo often leaves chic negative space and stains it with one violent hue.

Dutch Angle is a tilt. Giallo uses the tilt as one tool among gels and zooms.

Hyper-SaturationFeeling is louder than fact.

Dutch AngleThe world is off its axis. Do not use as decoration.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Suspiria (1977): colored glass as motivated key, dance-school architecture as a trap. Deep Red: zoomed inserts, primary interiors, investigation as fashion-horror.

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Giallo look on [Subject], hyper-saturated primaries, gelled window key, black leather implied in the foreground, 35mm zoom threat, Argento color crime. Name the red, green, or cobalt source.

Do not prompt a black-and-white alley.

Use in Image Generator

Giallo look on [Subject], hyper-saturated primaries, black leather gloves implied, Argento color crime, beauty as threat.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Film Noir or plain Hyper-Saturation: a fedora night, or a loud grade with no glove, no gelled window, and no zoom. The tell is teal-orange rain or even, pretty color with no threat axis.

Fix: pick one primary as the key, dutch or zoom toward the threat, and put a dark fashion object in the foreground.

Questions

What is Giallo in film?

An Italian mystery-horror look: gelled primary color, fashion interiors, zooms, dutch angles, and stylized violence. The lighting is often glamorous. The threat arrives as a color and a glove.

Giallo vs Film Noir

Noir withholds with black and wet silver streets. Giallo attacks with red, green, and cobalt in designed interiors. Both can dutch the camera. Only giallo treats a window gel as the murder weapon.

When should I use Giallo?

When horror has to look like a fashion spread until the glove enters. Skip it for silver crime, for future neon investigation, or for busy ornament that is not a threat.

How do I prompt Giallo for AI image or video?

Write: Giallo look on [Subject], hyper-saturated primaries, gelled window key, black leather in the foreground, 35mm zoom implied. Name the primary. Do not ask for noir silver or a generic saturated grade.

entries.title: Spaghetti Western
entries.text:
Spaghetti Western

Spaghetti western cinematography restages western iconography on Techniscope 2.35: dusty ochre landscapes, hard sun as the only key, and cuts from a 24mm plaza wide to a telephoto extreme close-up of eyes. Moral ambiguity sits in the hold on a face before anyone draws.

Create this Spaghetti Western

Narrative function

Myth is dirt, sweat, and a horizon that refuses shade. The sun is a weapon.

A Cowboy Shot shows the holster. An Extreme Close-Up of the eyes shows the decision.

The land is wide. The soul is a few millimeters of iris.

It is the wrong tool for a clean studio western or a misted martial landscape. American A-westerns often fill the faces and keep the sky polite.

Wuxia uses silk, mist, and wire, not ochre and hard noon.

How it works

35 spherical. Pair a 24mm or 28mm for the town and ridge with a 75mm to 135mm (historically much longer) for the eye.

Hard sun as key, little or no fill, dust as diffusion. Grade: burnt umber, bleached sky, dry highlights.

Blocking: hip-level cowboy size for guns, then the operatic hold on the face. Prompt Techniscope grit, dusty ochre, extreme close-ups of eyes, sun as a weapon.

When to use it

Use it when a standoff needs dirt, a hard sun, and a cut from landscape to iris. Do not use it for a polished sunset ride or for martial-arts mist.

Compared with similar shots

Spaghetti Western is hard sun, ochre, Techniscope, and eye ECUs. Cowboy Shot is only the size (mid-thigh).

Extreme Close-Up is only the size of the eye. Hard Light is the source.

The look is those tools in a dusty, morally dirty western, not a filled Hollywood campfire. Wuxia is the cousin in landscape myth with the opposite weather.

Cowboy ShotShow hands, weapons, or stance without going full body.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

In film

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (plaza wides against eye close-ups, bleached sun). Once Upon a Time in the West (operatic holds, Harmonica's face as a landscape).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

35, dusty ochre, hard noon sun, no fill, extreme close-up of eyes cut against a 24mm ridge. Name the dust and the holster height.

Do not prompt a clean golden-hour poster western.

Use in Image Generator

Spaghetti-western frame of [Subject], Techniscope grit, dusty ochre, extreme close-ups of eyes, sun as a weapon.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a glossy adventure western or Wuxia: rim-lit horses, polite skies, or bamboo mist. The tell is filled faces, teal-orange grade, and no eye ECU.

Fix: kill the fill, bleach the sky, add dust, and jump from a wide plaza to the eyes.

Questions

What is Spaghetti Western in film?

A western look built in Italy and Spain: Techniscope wides, hard sun, ochre dust, cowboy-size gun coverage, and telephoto eyes. The rhythm is operatic. The morals are dirty.

Spaghetti Western vs Wuxia

Both use landscape as myth. Spaghetti western is dry, hard, and ochre, with eye close-ups. Wuxia is mist, silk, and wire-assisted paths. Different weather, different lens pair.

When should I use Spaghetti Western?

When a standoff or a ridge arrival needs dirt and an unfilled sun. Skip it for martial mist, for IMAX-clean adventure gloss, or for night neon crime.

How do I prompt Spaghetti Western for AI image or video?

Write: Spaghetti-western frame of [Subject], Techniscope grit, dusty ochre, hard sun, no fill, extreme close-up of eyes, cowboy-shot holster. Do not ask for a clean sunset poster.

entries.title: Found Footage
entries.text:
Found Footage

Recovered recordingCamera as a story object

The found footage look presents images as a recording made by someone inside the events, often later discovered or assembled, so the camera is a story object with a timestamp, a battery, and a reason to keep rolling. Consumer digital, Hi8, or MiniDV optics, autofocus hunt, and amateur framing are constraints, not decoration.

Volume

Create this Found Footage

Narrative function

Knowledge is limited to what the operator can point at. What the camera misses is part of the beat.

Autofocus hunts a doorway. A timestamp sits in the corner.

The person holding the camera is in danger too, which is why the frame is late, dirty, and incomplete. Handheld footage alone is not found footage.

If there is no fictional origin for the tape, you have Handheld or stylistic suck. If a documentary crew is interviewing, you have documentary rhetoric, not a recovered camcorder.

How it works

Choose the device: Hi8, MiniDV, early digital, or a phone. Match its wide-ish zoom, auto exposure pumping, rolling shutter, and focus hunt.

Keep a plausible operator position and a reason the camera stays on. Night-vision is a mode of that device, not a grade.

Do not add a crane or a pretty close-up the operator could not have taken. Prompt consumer digital or Hi8, timestamp, autofocus hunt, amateur framing, and documentary panic as the operator's, not the film's.

When to use it

Use it when the operator is inside the event and the tape could later be found. Do not use shake as the entire premise, and do not use it for an omniscient amateur look with no diegetic camera.

Compared with similar shots

Found footage needs a diegetic recorder. Handheld is a body-mounted tool in an otherwise omniscient film.

Stylistic Suck can look cheap without a recovered-tape story. Cinéma vérité puts a filmmaker in real life as a catalyst, not a character's camcorder.

Night Vision is one mode the found camera may switch into. Documentary uses interview and observation, not a lost tape.

HandheldUrgency, documentary truth, or a mind that cannot sit still.

Night VisionSomeone is hunting in the dark.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

The Blair Witch Project (recordings presented as the missing filmmakers' tapes). REC (a television crew's camera as the constrained record).

Cloverfield (a personal camcorder framing a disaster). Grammar, not frames to copy.

The Blair Witch Project 1999The narrative is presented as recordings made by the missing filmmakers.

REC 2007A television crew’s camera becomes the constrained record of events.

Cloverfield 2008Personal recording frames the disaster experience.

Zelig 1983New material is integrated into an archival-looking documentary world.

The Battle of Algiers 1966The image evokes newsreel immediacy despite being staged.

Prompt it

Found-footage camera on [Subject], consumer digital or Hi8, timestamp, autofocus hunt, amateur framing, operator-height, documentary panic. Name who holds the camera and why it stays on.

Do not add a second, prettier angle.

Use in Video Generator

A volunteer records the final inventory of a closing observatory on a handheld camcorder. Every shot must have a plausible recording reason. When an unexplained door opens, the operator first documents the room number, then hesitates before following. Maintain limited battery, imperfect framing and consistent microphone perspective.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Handheld shake or Stylistic Suck ugliness with no operator. The tell is a perfect close-up, a crane, or coverage the character could not have shot.

Fix: pick the device, keep one operator position, let focus hunt, and let the frame miss the action.

Questions

What is Found Footage in film?

A narrative that presents images as recordings made by someone inside the fictional events, often discovered afterward. The camera's limits (timestamp, battery, autofocus, amateur framing) are the grammar.

Found Footage vs Handheld

Handheld is how the camera is held. Found footage is who owns the tape. You can have a stable found camera (a shelf cam, a news rig). Shake without a diegetic recorder is not found footage.

When should I use Found Footage?

When the operator is in the scene and the story depends on what that device can and cannot see. Skip it for omniscient cheapness, for sit-down interviews, or for any shot the character could not have taken.

How do I prompt Found Footage for AI image or video?

Write: Found-footage camera on [Subject], consumer digital or Hi8, timestamp, autofocus hunt, amateur framing. Name the operator and why the camera stays on. Do not request a second angle or a crane.

entries.title: Cinéma Vérité
entries.text:
Cinéma Vérité

Cinéma vérité uses available light, zoom-to-find framing, and the filmmaker's presence as a catalyst, so the camera is admitted into the room rather than hidden. Unpretty 16mm or digital frames, mixed color temperature, and a zoom hunting the moment are the physical signature, not a recovered amateur tape.

Create this Cinéma Vérité

Narrative function

Life is not staged for a key light. Someone talks, the zoom finds them, a window or a practical is the source, and the filmmaker's question or proximity changes what happens.

The frame can be late, centered wrong, or blown at the window. That is the contract.

It is the wrong tool when polish is the point, or when a fictional camcorder is the story. Blockbuster Gloss would be propaganda here.

Found footage needs a diegetic operator in danger. Documentary is broader: interviews, archive, and observation that may sit back.

How it works

Available light only, or a small on-camera bounce that still reads as room light. 16mm or a long ENG zoom (the 12-120 class), hunting focus and size.

Handheld or a monopod, eye height, reacting. Leave mixed tungsten and daylight.

Do not add a rim or a pretty backlight. Prompt available light, unpretty frames, zooming to find, life unstaged.

When to use it

Use it when style would feel like a lie and the filmmaker's presence is part of the event. Do not use it as a shake filter on a scripted scene that still has three-point lighting.

Compared with similar shots

Cinéma vérité is intervention and available light in documentary reality. Documentary includes sit-down interviews and archive.

French New Wave borrows the tools for fiction, then adds jump cuts and cinephile blocking. Handheld is only the body.

Available Light is only the source. Found Footage invents a tape inside the story.

HandheldUrgency, documentary truth, or a mind that cannot sit still.

Available LightCommit to the hour you have.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Don't Look Back (zoom-to-find, dressing rooms, a public figure not styled for film). Primary (campaign interiors, available light, the camera in the room).

The Battle of Algiers (newsreel immediacy as a staged cousin of this grammar). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Cinéma vérité treatment of [Subject], available light, unpretty frames, zooming to find, mixed color temperature, life unstaged. Name the window or practical.

Do not add a rim, a crane, or a recovered-tape timestamp.

Use in Image Generator

Cinéma vérité treatment of [Subject], available light, unpretty frames, zooming to find, life unstaged.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Found Footage or pretty Documentary: a timestamp and panic, or a keyed interview with a clean backlight. The tell is three-point light, a rim, or a device story.

Fix: kill the film lights, let the zoom hunt, and keep the filmmaker in the room as a presence, not a horror operator.

Questions

What is Cinéma Vérité in film?

A documentary look in which available light, zoom-to-find framing, and the filmmaker's presence provoke or witness unstaged life. The camera is a catalyst, not a hidden observer with a key and a rim.

Cinéma Vérité vs Documentary

Documentary is a broad rhetoric: interview, archive, observation, even mock forms. Cinéma vérité is a specific physical method: available light, zoom, presence. A sit-down with a window key can be documentary without being vérité.

When should I use Cinéma Vérité?

When prettifying the room would feel like propaganda, and the filmmaker's being there matters. Skip it for recovered-tape horror, for billboard gloss, or for a scripted scene that still wants a rim light.

How do I prompt Cinéma Vérité for AI image or video?

Write: Cinéma vérité treatment of [Subject], available light, unpretty frames, zooming to find, mixed color, life unstaged. Name the real source. Do not add a timestamp, a rim, or a crane.

entries.text:
French New Wave

French New Wave cinematography shoots fiction on locations with street light, handheld 16mm or 35mm, and an edit that will jump-cut rather than cover. The frame jumps into walking life: cafes, sidewalks, apartments with mixed practicals, and a camera that admits it is a camera.

Create this French New Wave

Narrative function

Youth and impatience with studio polish. A character talks to the lens.

A walk is a burst of handheld, then a jump cut skips the boring meters. Paris oxygen, or any city's equivalent, is the lighting plot: windows, cafes, overcast streets.

It is not cinéma vérité. Vérité is documentary presence.

New Wave is authored fiction using documentary tools plus cinephile grammar (Jump Cut, freeze, iris, a look at the camera). It is also not found footage: there is no recovered tape, only a director in the street.

How it works

Location interiors, available or small practicals, 35mm or 50mm on a Cameflex-class body, handheld or a light tripod. Shoot the walk, then jump-cut in the edit.

Reflexive beats: eyeline to camera, a sudden insert. Street daylight, cafe tungsten, no matching backlight.

Prompt jump cuts implied, street light, jump-into-life framing, handheld Paris oxygen as location air, not as a mood word.

When to use it

Use it when a young, restless fiction needs streets, jump cuts, and impatience with coverage. Do not use it for studio three-point polish or for a camcorder-horror premise.

Compared with similar shots

French New Wave is fiction plus location plus Jump Cut. Cinéma Vérité is documentary catalysis.

Handheld is the body only. Documentary may interview.

New Wave characters still act a story. Arthouse may be slower, emptier, and less cinephile-playful.

The New Wave camera is in a hurry.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

HandheldUrgency, documentary truth, or a mind that cannot sit still.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Breathless (jump cuts on the street and in the room, a look to camera). The 400 Blows (location childhood, available light, a final run).

Cléo from 5 to 7 (real-time Paris, streets and interiors as a clock). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

French New Wave energy on [Subject], location street light, handheld 35mm, jump cuts implied, jump-into-life framing, mixed cafe practicals. Name the sidewalk or apartment.

Do not add a rim, a timestamp, or studio flags.

Use in Image Generator

French New Wave energy on [Subject], jump cuts implied, street light, jump-into-life framing, handheld Paris oxygen.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Cinéma Vérité or Found Footage: a documentary claim, or a tape. The tell is a news timestamp, a horror shake, or glossy three-point.

Fix: keep it fiction, keep it location, handheld or light tripod, and let the edit jump.

Questions

What is French New Wave in film?

A fiction look from late-1950s France and its heirs: location shooting, street and practical light, handheld cameras, jump cuts, and reflexive cinephile grammar. Studio polish is the enemy.

French New Wave vs Cinéma Vérité

Vérité documents real people and lets the filmmaker provoke. New Wave stages a story with the same cameras and streets, then jump-cuts and looks back at the lens. One is documentary method. The other is fiction with documentary tools.

When should I use French New Wave?

When a restless fiction belongs on a sidewalk or in a cheap apartment, and coverage would feel like a studio. Skip it for recovered-tape horror, for vérité documentary, or for billboard gloss.

entries.title: Wuxia
entries.text:
Wuxia

Wuxia cinematography stages martial chivalry in landscape: misted bamboo or desert silk, long-shot geography, and wire-assisted paths that read as weightless rather than as street punching. Color is costume and fog, not a gelled murder window.

Create this Wuxia

Narrative function

The fight is a poem in a real (or studio-built) landscape. A body travels a wire path through Mist.

A Long Shot keeps honor readable as choreography, not as a blur of impacts. Silk and banners carry hue.

The camera cranes or holds wide so the land remains the other actor. It is the wrong tool for a grit street fight or a dusty gun standoff.

Hong Kong urban kung fu wants handheld wides and hits. Spaghetti Western wants hard sun and eyes.

Wuxia wants weather, fabric, and a path through air.

How it works

35 spherical or anamorphic. 24mm to 40mm for wire wides, 50mm to 75mm to compress bamboo.

Mist or smoke as diffusion, not as a night-club haze. Crane, jib, or wire-rig the performer so the path has a rise and a float.

Slow the strike, not the walk. Palette: silk dyes, forest green, desert gold, color-coded armies if the story needs them.

Prompt misted bamboo, wire-fu weightlessness implied, silk color, heroic wides, Crouching Tiger air as weather, not as a slogan.

When to use it

Use it when martial myth needs landscape and a weightless path. Do not use it for a bar brawl, a gun standoff, or a handheld hit sequence.

Compared with similar shots

Wuxia is mist, silk, wire, and Long Shot geography. Spaghetti Western is ochre, hard sun, and eye close-ups.

Mist is the atmosphere only. Long Shot is the size only.

A street kung-fu look is the opposite: wide, close, dirty, and weighted. Do not swap them.

MistSofter mystery than fog. Lyric, not monster.

Long ShotPlace a human in a world that could ignore them.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (bamboo canopy, rooftop paths, wire as flight). Hero (color-coded armies, desert and lake as moral spaces).

House of Flying Daggers (forest, silk, and a fight that is also a dance). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Wuxia look on [Subject], misted bamboo or silk banners, wire-fu weightlessness implied, long-shot landscape, designed costume color, crane or wide hold. Name the weather and the path through air.

Do not prompt a dusty gunfight or a handheld alley brawl.

Use in Image Generator

Wuxia look on [Subject], misted bamboo, wire-fu weightlessness implied, silk color, heroic wides, Crouching Tiger air.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a grit martial film or Spaghetti Western: sweat, ochre, and punches, or a noon standoff. The tell is no mist, no wire path, and a camera in the fighters' faces.

Fix: widen up, add mist, show the path through air, and let costume carry color.

Questions

What is Wuxia in film?

A martial-chivalry look: landscape wides, mist or silk weather, wire-assisted weightless movement, and color as costume rather than as a gelled threat. The fight is staged as myth, not as a street beating.

Wuxia vs Spaghetti Western

Both mythologize landscape. Wuxia uses mist, silk, and wire paths. Spaghetti western uses hard sun, dust, and telephoto eyes. Different weather, different combat, different close-up.

When should I use Wuxia?

When a martial beat needs land, weather, and a floating path. Skip it for gun standoffs, for urban handheld fights, or for horror gels.

How do I prompt Wuxia for AI image or video?

entries.title: Tech Noir
entries.text:
Tech Noir

future noircyber-noircyber noir

Tech noir (also called future noir or cyber-noir) fuses noir's hard keys, rain, and guilty blocking with science-fiction production design: screens, LEDs, and corporate towers as practical sources. Analog crime grammar sits inside a digital city.

Create this Tech Noir

Narrative function

The future is wet and guilty. A detective, a fugitive, or a machine walks rain that is lit by advertisements and monitors.

The face is still half in shadow. The key is no longer only a streetlamp.

It is a billboard, a terminal, a police scanner. It is not all dystopia and not all neo-noir.

Dystopian can be daylight bureaucracy and civic scale with no crime plot. Neo-Noir can be a present-day parking garage with sodium lamps and no future tech.

Tech noir needs both the investigation geometry and the machine city.

How it works

Keep noir ratios: hard key, unfilled cheek, wet ground. Replace tungsten with screens and LEDs as motivated keys, plus residual sodium or neon.

Smoke or rain for volume. 35mm or 40mm anamorphic, night exteriors, occasional long-lens compression of towers.

Blocking: figures small under signage, then a close-up keyed by a display. Prompt future crime, screens as practicals, rain, corporate night, analog noir in a digital city.

When to use it

Use it when a future city is also a crime scene and the screens light the guilt. Do not use it for a clean utopian interface, or for present-day noir with no speculative design.

Compared with similar shots

Tech Noir is noir plus science-fiction sources. Neo-Noir is color noir without requiring future tech.

Dystopian is the used civic system, often in daylight, with the state as antagonist. Neon Practicals is the lamp.

Film Noir is the silver ancestor. If there is no screen, tower, or machine as light, you are still in neo-noir.

Neo-NoirNoir after color was invented.

Neon PracticalsThe city is the lighting department.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Blade Runner (rain, neon, and a detective plot inside a machine city). The Terminator (1984 night, tech-noir club and streets, analog crime against a future machine).

Ghost in the Shell (1995) (screens, rain, and investigation as identity). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Tech-noir on [Subject], future crime, screens as practicals, rain, corporate night, hard unfilled key, analog noir in a digital city. Name the display that lights the face.

Do not prompt a present-day alley with no speculative design.

Use in Image Generator

Tech-noir on [Subject], future crime, screens as practicals, rain, corporate night, analog noir in a digital city.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Neo-Noir or generic Dystopian: contemporary neon crime, or a grey megacity with no investigation geometry. The tell is no screen as a source, or daylight civic haze with no wet guilty night.

Fix: add a display key, rain, towers, and a crime blocking of isolation.

Questions

What is Tech Noir in film?

A fusion of noir lighting and crime structure with science-fiction design. Screens and corporate night become the practicals. Rain stays. Guilt stays. The city is digital. The grammar is still investigation.

Tech Noir vs Neo-Noir

Neo-noir is color noir in a later or present world. Tech noir requires speculative technology as light and as threat. Blade Runner is both. A 2010s parking-garage crime film may be neo-noir only.

When should I use Tech Noir?

When the future is a wet crime scene and a screen lights the face. Skip it for silver 1940s noir, for daylight civic dystopia, or for pastel vaporwave with no investigation.

How do I prompt Tech Noir for AI image or video?

Write: Tech-noir on [Subject], future crime, screens as practicals, rain, corporate night, hard unfilled key. Name the display. Do not stop at neon rain with no speculative city.

entries.title: Southern Gothic
entries.text:
Southern Gothic

Southern Gothic cinema

Southern gothic cinematography uses the American South as a humid optical problem: late-afternoon gold gone sickly, Spanish-moss Dappled Light, porch tungsten, and Atmospheric Haze that keeps heat in the air. Decay is on the walls. The threat is family, history, and something under the porch, not a city streetlamp.

Create this Southern Gothic

Narrative function

Beauty is rotting. A house peels.

Sweat holds on skin. Sun through moss becomes a moving gobo.

The palette is gold-green and tobacco, not cyan neon. Blocking is slow: a porch, a church, a river, a dinner table that will not end.

It is the wrong tool for urban night crime or for cosmic scale. Film Noir is a wet city.

Cosmic horror makes the human irrelevant against illegal geometry. Southern gothic keeps the human too close: kin, pulpit, swamp.

How it works

Late sun as key, often raking, through trees or moss so the pattern crawls. Add atmospheric haze or real humidity so blacks go milky.

Porch bulbs and interior practicals go warm and a little dirty. 35mm or 50mm spherical, sometimes 24mm for a house against sky.

Avoid clean rims. Let paint peel in the highlight.

Prompt humid decay, moss, late-afternoon gold gone sickly, beauty rotting as production design, not as a slogan.

When to use it

Use it when heat, family, and decay have to be visible in the air. Do not use it as generic gothic fog on a Victorian stone castle, or as noir in a Southern town with the humidity removed.

Compared with similar shots

Southern Gothic is humid gold-green decay. Dappled Light is the moss gobo only.

Atmospheric Haze is the air only. Cosmic Horror is scale and illegal geometry.

Film Noir is urban night silver. A British gothic look is stone, grey, and cold.

Keep the heat.

Dappled LightNature or blinds as gobo.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

The Night of the Hunter (river, moonlight, and a Southern fable's hard shadows). Beasts of the Southern Wild (humid daylight, water, a community at the edge of weather).

True Detective S1 (sickly gold, industrial coast, family rot). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Southern gothic air around [Subject], humid decay, Spanish moss dappled sun, late-afternoon gold gone sickly, porch tungsten, peeling paint. Name the heat and the house.

Do not prompt a dry noir alley or a cosmic void.

Use in Image Generator

Southern gothic air around [Subject], humid decay, moss, late-afternoon gold gone sickly, beauty rotting.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Film Noir or generic gothic fog: wet city silver, or a cold castle. The tell is no humidity, no moss pattern, and a teal night grade.

Fix: add late sickly sun, haze, peeling surfaces, and slow porch blocking.

Questions

What is Southern Gothic in film?

A look that makes the American South's heat, decay, and haunted social history optical: sickly gold, moss dapples, humidity, porch practicals, and slow blocking around family and land.

Southern Gothic vs Cosmic Horror

Southern gothic keeps human kin too close: a porch, a pulpit, a swamp. Cosmic horror shrinks the human against wrong scale and geometry. One is family rot. The other is the universe refusing you.

When should I use Southern Gothic?

When heat, family, and something under the porch must be visible. Skip it for urban noir, for future rain, or for a cold stone gothic with no humidity.

How do I prompt Southern Gothic for AI image or video?

Write: Southern gothic air around [Subject], humid decay, moss, late-afternoon gold gone sickly, porch tungsten, peeling paint. Name the house and the heat. Do not ask for a wet city or a cosmic void.

entries.title: Cosmic Horror
entries.text:
Cosmic Horror

Lovecraftian horrorcosmic dread

Cosmic horror cinematography builds dread from human insignificance: extreme long shots, slightly illegal geometry, under-light on faces, and a brightness that reveals too much. The threat is not a man. Scale, entity, and knowledge that will not fit a face are the optical problem.

Create this Cosmic Horror

Narrative function

The frame makes the person a mistake. A horizon does not match.

A structure has too many vanishing points. Light may be too hard, too colored, or too revealing, so looking is the harm.

Underlighting turns a familiar face into a specimen. It is the wrong tool for a slasher in a cabin or for family rot on a porch.

Giallo is a gloved human. Southern Gothic is kin and heat.

Cosmic horror needs the universe, a lab, an ice, a shimmer, or a ship that is also a geometry error.

How it works

Start too wide: Extreme Long Shot of land, ice, or a structure that is the wrong size. Cheat perspective (forced, dutch, non-matching vanishing points) a little, not as cartoon expressionism.

Light faces from below or from a source that has no sun logic. Overexpose the revelation.

Palette: Antarctic bounce, alien shimmer, or red that is not a gel gag. Prompt scale wrong, geometry slightly illegal, a brightness that reveals too much, human irrelevance.

When to use it

Use it when the threat cannot be a person and the image must make knowledge dangerous. Do not use it for a masked killer in a hallway, or for a foggy swamp that is still a family story.

Compared with similar shots

Cosmic horror is scale, illegal geometry, and revealing light. Extreme Long Shot is only size.

Underlighting is only the angle. German Expressionism bends sets as a mind; cosmic horror bends them as an alien fact.

Southern Gothic keeps humans too near. Dreamcore is a soft liminal room, not a cosmos.

Extreme Long ShotScale is the emotion.

UnderlightingThe source is fire, a screen on the floor, or a monster.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

The Thing (1982): Antarctic bounce, isolation wides, a body that will not stay a body. Annihilation: shimmer, wrong color in daylight, landscape as mutation.

Event Horizon: a ship interior whose lighting and geometry refuse comfort. Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Cosmic horror framing of [Subject], scale wrong, geometry slightly illegal, under-lit face or a brightness that reveals too much, human irrelevance, extreme long shot or a corridor that does not vanish correctly. Do not prompt a gloved killer.

Use in Image Generator

Cosmic horror framing of [Subject], scale wrong, geometry slightly illegal, a brightness that reveals too much, human irrelevance.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a slasher, Southern Gothic, or generic fog. The tell is a human antagonist filling the frame, or a porch.

Fix: widen until the person is small, break one vanishing point, and let the source be too bright or from below.

Questions

What is Cosmic Horror in film?

A look that makes humans optically irrelevant: wrong scale, slightly illegal geometry, under-light or over-revealing brightness, and a threat that is not a person. Knowledge is the harm.

Cosmic Horror vs Southern Gothic

Southern gothic traps you in kin, heat, and a house. Cosmic horror traps you in a universe that will not parse. One is too close. The other is too large and too wrong.

When should I use Cosmic Horror?

When the antagonist cannot be a man and looking is dangerous. Skip it for slashers, for family decay, for giallo gloves, or for a foggy swamp with a human in it.

How do I prompt Cosmic Horror for AI image or video?

Write: Cosmic horror framing of [Subject], scale wrong, geometry slightly illegal, a brightness that reveals too much, human irrelevance. Name the horizon error. Do not ask for a masked killer.

entries.title: Vaporwave
entries.text:
Vaporwave

The vaporwave aesthetic is a pastel, low-contrast look: pink-cyan gradients, marble and palms, mall fluorescents, and VHS chroma bleed, as if a 1980s future never shipped. The camera is often centered and still. There is no crime geometry unless you add it.

Create this Vaporwave

Narrative function

Nostalgia for a catalog that closed. A bust, a grid floor, Japanese retail signage, a sunset that is a gradient more than a sun.

Highlights bloom like consumer tape. The mood is mall-at-closing, not investigation.

It is easy to confuse with Neo-Noir because both like cyan and magenta. Noir still wants a hard key, rain guilt, and a face in shadow.

Vaporwave wants even pastel fill, sculpture, and tape artifacts. Cross Process can supply the hue shift.

It is not the whole look.

How it works

Soft, even sources: fluorescent mall, plus a pink or cyan gel as a wash, not a hard key. Center the subject.

35mm spherical, moderate depth. Add VHS: chroma bleed, slight tracking error, soft resolution.

Set dressing: marble, palms, Greek busts, grid, sunset gradient. Prompt pink-cyan gradient, marble and palms, VHS bleed, mall-at-closing melancholy as empty retail air, not as a slogan.

When to use it

Use it when the image should feel like a unused future on worn tape. Do not use it as a crime night or as a hard neon-noir alley.

Compared with similar shots

Vaporwave is pastel, centered, and tape-soft. Neo-Noir is hard, rainy, and guilty.

Neon Practicals is the tube. Cross Process is a chemical hue shift.

Tech Noir still investigates. If the face is unfilled and the street is wet, you have left the mall.

Cross ProcessWrong chemistry on purpose.

Neon PracticalsThe city is the lighting department.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Drive supplies adjacent night grammar (pink-cyan practicals) but remains neo-noir in blocking. The look itself is more native to music video and internet stills than to a single film cycle.

Use Drive only as a cousin for hue, not as a crime template.

Prompt it

Vaporwave treatment of [Subject], pink-cyan gradient, marble and palms, VHS bleed, centered 35mm, mall fluorescent fill, no hard unfilled cheek. Name the bust or the grid.

Do not prompt a wet detective alley.

Use in Image Generator

Vaporwave treatment of [Subject], pink-cyan gradient, marble and palms, VHS bleed, mall-at-closing melancholy.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Neo-Noir: rain, hard key, raincoat. The tell is an unfilled cheek and wet asphalt.

Fix: flatten the contrast, center the frame, add marble or palms, and let VHS chroma bleed the edges.

Questions

What is Vaporwave in film?

A pastel look of pink-cyan wash, marble, palms, mall light, and VHS bleed. It nostalgizes a retail future that never arrived. It is not a crime lighting plot unless you force one.

Vaporwave vs Neo-Noir

Both may use cyan and magenta. Neo-noir keeps hard keys, rain, and isolation. Vaporwave keeps even fill, sculpture, and tape softness. Hue overlap is not the same look.

When should I use Vaporwave?

When the beat is unused-future nostalgia on consumer tape. Skip it for investigation, for hard rain, or for early-web horror (that is Weirdcore).

How do I prompt Vaporwave for AI image or video?

Write: Vaporwave treatment of [Subject], pink-cyan gradient, marble and palms, VHS bleed, centered 35mm, mall fluorescent fill. Do not add a hard unfilled noir cheek.

entries.title: Documentary
entries.text:
Documentary

Fictional documentaryDocumentary parody

Documentary cinematography mixes observational coverage with interview and archive rhetoric: unstyled wardrobe light, mixed color temperatures, a zoom finding focus, and respect without a glamour rim. Fictional films may borrow the same grammar as mockumentary. That is still documentary rhetoric, not a recovered camcorder tape.

Volume

Create this Documentary

Narrative function

The camera claims evidence. A sit-down by a window.

A wide of work being done. A cutaway that pretends to prove the sentence.

Comedy and unease both live in the gap between what people say and what the camera appears to witness. It is broader than Cinéma Vérité.

Vérité hunts with a zoom and admits the filmmaker as catalyst. Documentary may also plant a stable interview, use archive, or build a fictional crew (Interview style, observational B-roll).

It is not Found Footage: there is usually an implied production, not a lost tape.

How it works

Leave mixed color. Window key for interviews, 35mm to 50mm, eye level, interviewer often offscreen.

Observational wides on a zoom, focus hunting is allowed if the implied crew would hunt. No hair light unless the real room has one.

Imperfect coverage only when it fits that production. Prompt mixed color, unstyled wardrobe light, zoom finding focus, respect without glamour.

When to use it

Use it when pretty would be a lie, or when a fiction wants interview-versus-observation irony. Do not use it as random shake, and do not swap it for a recovered-camera story.

Compared with similar shots

Documentary is a rhetoric (interview, observation, archive). Cinéma Vérité is a method (available light, presence, zoom-to-find).

Found Footage is a diegetic recorder. Available Light is the source only.

BTS shows a film set's crew. Mockumentary uses documentary rhetoric on invented people.

Quality check: those are not interchangeable.

Cinéma VéritéStyle would be propaganda.

Available LightCommit to the hour you have.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

The Act of Killing (reenactment and interview as evidence). Honeyland (observational patience, mixed natural light).

Won't You Be My Neighbor? (archive plus sit-down).

This Is Spinal Tap and Best in Show (fictional crews using interview and observation). Grammar, not frames to copy.

This Is Spinal Tap 1984Interviews, backstage observation and performance footage construct the fictional band’s story.

Best in Show 2000Interviews and observational scenes build the dog-show ensemble.

Prompt it

Documentary look on [Subject], mixed color, unstyled wardrobe light, zoom finding focus, interview or observational coverage, respect without glamour. Name whether this is a sit-down or a follow.

Do not add a timestamp or a rim.

Use in Video Generator

Create a short mockumentary about a municipal committee preparing the world’s smallest parade. Intercut confident seated interviews with observational footage of tiny practical setbacks. Keep interview framing consistent, interviewer mostly offscreen and comedy grounded in sincere behavior rather than broad reaction faces.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Found Footage or glossy interview: a horror camcorder, or a keyed talk show. The tell is a timestamp, or a Hollywood hair light on a 'documentary' subject.

Fix: pick a crew style, mix the color, and let the zoom or the window be the only flattery.

Questions

What is Documentary in film?

A look and a rhetoric: observational wides, sit-down interviews, archive, mixed color, and unstyled light. Fiction can wear the same clothes (mockumentary) without becoming found footage.

Documentary vs Cinéma Vérité

Vérité is one documentary method: presence, available light, zoom-to-find. Documentary as a look also includes stable interviews and archive. A window-keyed sit-down can be documentary and still not be vérité.

When should I use Documentary?

When the image must look like evidence, or when a fiction needs the gap between testimony and observation. Skip it for recovered-tape horror, for vérité-only catalysis, or for glamour rims.

How do I prompt Documentary for AI image or video?

entries.title: Blockbuster Gloss
entries.text:
Blockbuster Gloss

Blockbuster cinematography is high-contrast, billboard-readable coverage: clean skies or designed weather, a heroic rim on hair and shoulder, volumetric shafts, and a grade that often splits teal shadow from warm skin. The shot must still parse at poster size.

Create this Blockbuster Gloss

Narrative function

Adventure as a still that could sell the film. Faces are shaped.

Horizons are clean. Dust and haze exist to carry god-rays, not to hide information.

39 anamorphic, but the finish is expensive contrast, not empty duration. It is the wrong tool when thought needs space or when cheapness is the truth.

Arthouse leaves headroom and waits. Stylistic Suck would be dishonest here in reverse: polish is the contract.

Teal and Orange is a grade you can apply to anything. Gloss is the whole package: rim, scale, cleanliness.

How it works

Key plus a strong backlight rim. Add haze for Volumetric Light shafts.

Keep skies clean or dramatically designed, not stained by accident. 24mm to 40mm for scale, longer glass for faces if the format is large.

Use it when the shot must play on a billboard and the world should look funded. Do not use it for a quiet empty interior, a vérité interview, or a decaying porch.

Compared with similar shots

Blockbuster Gloss is rim, scale, and clean contrast. Teal and Orange is only the grade.

Volumetric Light is only the shaft. Arthouse is the opposite contract: patience and empty frame.

Maximalism packs pattern. Gloss can be relatively simple, just expensive.

Dystopian dirties the civic future. Gloss polishes the adventure.

A large-scale adventure finish: high contrast, clean or designed weather, a heroic rim, volumetric shafts, and billboard-readable geography. The image is built to sell and to parse far from the screen.

Blockbuster Gloss vs Arthouse

Gloss fills and shapes: rim, contrast, poster horizon. Arthouse leaves space, odd headroom, and duration. One is afraid of emptiness. The other uses emptiness as the point.

When should I use Blockbuster Gloss?

entries.title: Arthouse
entries.text:
Arthouse

Arthouse cinematography leaves space for thought: a Static Locked-Off camera, odd Headroom, natural or window light, and a frame willing to be empty. Duration is implied even in a still. The picture does not sell itself as a poster.

Create this Arthouse

Narrative function

Someone sits. The room keeps being a room.

Headroom is a little wrong. The light is a window, not a rim.

You are allowed to get bored, which is how thought enters. Negative space is not a mistake.

It is the wrong tool when the shot must play on a billboard or when the camera should hunt. Blockbuster Gloss shapes every edge.

French New Wave is impatient and jump-cut. Photography may also hold still, but as a print: posed, decisive, often centered.

Arthouse can be off-center, slightly ugly, and long.

How it works

Lock the tripod. 35mm or 50mm spherical, modest stop, available or window key, little or no fill.

Allow odd headroom and Negative Space. Do not add a backlight rim unless the room has one.

Color stays mixed or quietly naturalistic. Prompt patience, odd headroom, natural light, the frame willing to be empty, duration implied.

When to use it

Use it when a beat needs time and air more than emphasis. Do not use it on an action geography pass, and do not confuse it with a centered stills-like tableau.

Compared with similar shots

Arthouse is empty, patient, and often slightly mis-framed. Blockbuster Gloss is the opposite finish.

Negative Space is a composition tool. Static Locked-Off is the locked camera.

Photography pretends to be a print: posed light, decisive moment. Arthouse may refuse the decisive moment and keep running.

Negative SpaceLoneliness needs room.

Static Locked-OffTrust blocking and duration. Movement would be noise.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Toni Erdmann (plain light, social duration, frames that do not flatter). Roma (65mm black-and-white patience, even when the set is full).

Drive My Car (holds on cars, rooms, and grief). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Blockbuster Gloss or Photography: a rim-lit poster, or a perfectly posed print. The tell is a hair light, centered beauty, and no empty duration.

Fix: lock off, raise the headroom, kill the rim, and let the room stay a room.

Questions

What is Arthouse in film?

A patient look: locked camera, odd headroom, natural light, and a willingness to be empty. The frame leaves time for thought instead of selling a poster.

Arthouse vs Blockbuster Gloss

Arthouse withholds polish and fills the frame with air. Blockbuster gloss rims, contrasts, and designs the sky so the still could sell tickets. Choose based on whether emptiness is allowed.

When should I use Arthouse?

When a scene needs space and duration more than emphasis. Skip it for action posters, for vérité hunting zooms, or for a posed photographic tableau that wants to be a print.

entries.title: Animation
entries.text:
Animation

Animation cinematography constructs light and motion instead of capturing them: graphic volume, designed keys, and movement as drawing, paint, or stepped CG, not as a photographed exposure. The world is built. Lens physics appear only if you choose them.

Create this Animation

Narrative function

A drawing can hold a smear. A painted film can ignore a 180-degree shutter.

Spider-Verse can step the action and print halftone. Kaguya can let charcoal dissolve.

The 'camera' is a viewpoint in a constructed space. It is not Pixel Art (discrete sampling and a locked palette) and not Stop Motion (physical puppets moved a frame at a time).

Those are specific construction methods. Animation as a look means designed light and graphic motion, in 2D, 3D, or hybrid.

How it works

Decide the construction: 2D volumes, CG with graphic shaders, or mixed. Light is keyed in the design, not motivated only by a set practical unless you invent one.

Motion: smears, holds, stepped frame rates, or full 24fps. Do not default to photoreal ray-traced blur unless that is the film.

Prompt graphic volume, designed light, motion as drawing rather than photography.

When to use it

Use it when the world must be constructed, not captured. Do not use it as a filter on live action that still wants real lens physics, and do not collapse it into pixel tiles or puppet stop-motion unless that is the method.

Compared with similar shots

Animation is constructed motion and light. Pixel Art is tiled, paletted sampling.

Stop Motion is physical increment. Video Game is playable camera logic (follow cam, HUD, collision), which may be animated or live-action dressed as a game.

A photoreal CG shot that imitates a 50mm still is animation as production, not this graphic look.

Pixel ArtThe world is tiles.

Stop MotionMotion should feel made.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (stepped motion, graphic halftone, designed light). The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (charcoal and watercolor as cinematography).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Do not ask for photoreal lens bokeh unless that is the construction.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is photoreal live action, Pixel Art, or Stop Motion. The tell is a 50mm bokeh plate, chunky sprites, or puppet seams you did not want.

Fix: specify the graphic medium, design the key as paint or shader, and choose smear or stepped motion.

Questions

What is Animation in film?

A constructed look: light and motion are designed (drawn, painted, or shaded), not captured through a lens, unless you deliberately simulate a lens. Graphic volume replaces photographic exposure.

Animation vs Pixel Art

Pixel art locks sampling and palette into visible tiles. Animation may be fluid charcoal, cel, or graphic 3D. Both are constructed. Only pixel art makes the pixel the unit of the world.

When should I use Animation?

When the world cannot or should not be a photographed place. Skip it if you want a real lens, if you want visible tiles, or if you want puppet stop-motion specifically.

entries.title: BTS
entries.text:
BTS

Behind the scenes cinematography shows the making: C-stands, flags, the set wall, and crew in the same frame as the fiction, so the constructed world leaks. Documentary light (worklamps, mixed Kinos) sits beside the scene's key.

Create this BTS

Narrative function

The shot admits the apparatus. An actor holds a mark.

A boom dips. The apartment has no fourth wall.

You came for the scene and got the factory that makes it. That leak can be comic, tender, or cruel.

It is not Cinéma Vérité of real life, and not a sit-down Interview unless you plant one on the set. It is documentary rhetoric aimed at a film set.

Documentary of a non-film subject will not show stands and flags.

How it works

Two lighting worlds: the scene's motivated key on the actor, and unstyled worklight on crew and the studio. Include a stand, a flag, a slate, or the unfinished set edge.

Camera: observational handheld or a wider locked shot that keeps crew readable. Do not pretty the crew with the movie rim.

Prompt crew, stands, and the set edge visible, the fiction leaking, documentary light on a constructed world.

When to use it

Use it when the making must be visible, not only the make-believe. Do not use it as a vérité street look with no set, and do not hide every stand if you claimed BTS.

Compared with similar shots

BTS is a set with its crew visible. Cinéma Vérité is real life with a filmmaker.

Documentary is evidence rhetoric at large. Interview may appear inside BTS (a director talk) but is not the leak of the set.

If there is no apparatus in frame, it is not behind the scenes.

Cinéma VéritéStyle would be propaganda.

InterviewSomeone is answering a question we did not hear.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Day for Night (a production as the subject, the set as a factory). Living in Oblivion (independent-set chaos as comedy).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Do not hide the apparatus.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Cinéma Vérité or a clean production still: street vérité, or the scene with no crew. The tell is a finished fourth wall and no stands.

Fix: show the wall missing, a flag, a person with a boom, and mixed worklight.

Questions

What is BTS in film?

Behind-the-scenes coverage: crew, stands, and the unfinished set visible in the same frame as the fiction. Documentary light on a constructed world, so the making leaks.

BTS vs Cinéma Vérité

Vérité watches unstaged life. BTS watches a set. Both may be handheld and mixed-color. Only BTS needs C-stands, flags, and a missing fourth wall as the subject.

When should I use BTS?

When the story or the still must show the making. Skip it for recovered-tape horror, for street vérité with no set, or for a finished scene with the apparatus hidden.

entries.title: Dreamcore
entries.text:
Dreamcore

The dreamcore aesthetic is a soft, liminal interior look: empty rooms, pools, and suburban halls lit by childhood practicals gone slightly wrong, with low contrast and unresolved space. Nostalgia is present. Safety is not.

Create this Dreamcore

Narrative function

A corridor continues too far. A fluorescent is a little green.

A window is over-bloomed like a memory. The person may be small or absent.

Nothing jumps. The dread is that the room will not resolve into a place you can leave.

It is not Weirdcore (low-res digital, captions, early-web jokes that threaten). It is not Altered State (smear, afterimage, unhooked color as perception failure).

It is not Magical Realism (a recognizable world with one impossible fact treated as weather). Dreamcore is the memory-room.

How it works

Wide 24mm to 35mm, eye level, often locked. Soft sources: fluorescent, a cheap tungsten lamp, a blown window.

Keep contrast low. Fog the blacks a little.

Palette: 1990s suburban pastel or pool cyan, slightly sick. Empty the mid-ground.

Prompt liminal rooms, soft dread, childhood lighting gone wrong, a memory that will not resolve.

When to use it

Use it when nostalgia must lose its safety in an empty interior. Do not use it for JPEG horror, for a miracle in daylight realism, or for a warped trip sequence.

Compared with similar shots

Dreamcore is soft analog liminal space. Weirdcore is degraded digital and captioned.

Altered State warps the image physically. Magical Realism keeps ordinary light and one impossible fact.

If you add clipart and 240p, you have left dreamcore.

WeirdcoreThe familiar is incorrectly rendered.

Altered StateThe mind is the location.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Synecdoche, New York (rooms that replicate and will not end, theater as a memory warehouse). The Backrooms culture (liminal empty interiors as internet folklore).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Do not add JPEG captions or psychedelic smear.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Weirdcore or Altered State: chunky artifacts and captions, or trailing edges. The tell is low-res clipart or a trip warp.

Fix: keep resolution continuous, soften the key, empty the corridor, and let the light be almost-childhood.

Questions

What is Dreamcore in film?

A liminal, soft-interior look: empty rooms, childhood practicals gone wrong, low contrast, and unresolved space. Nostalgia remains. Safety does not.

Dreamcore vs Weirdcore

Dreamcore is analog-soft and spatial. Weirdcore is early-web: low-res, cropped, captioned, a joke that threatens. One is a room you almost remember. The other is a file you should not have opened.

When should I use Dreamcore?

When an empty interior must feel like a memory with the safety removed. Skip it for captioned JPEG horror, for perception smear, or for a daylight miracle in a real town.

entries.title: Dystopian
entries.text:
Dystopian

Dystopian cinematography makes the civic system the antagonist: used architecture, haze, rank, and signage at a scale that already feels worn. The future is not shiny. It is bureaucratic, polluted, or monumental and cold, often in daylight as well as night.

Create this Dystopian

Narrative function

A checkpoint. A tower.

A crowd compressed by a long lens, or a handheld walk through trash and concrete. The sky is rarely clean.

The person is ranked by clothing, by queue, by a logo on a wall. It is not automatically Tech Noir.

Tech noir is wet guilty night and investigation, screens as keys. Dystopia can be a grey afternoon, a refugee camp, an orange industrial fog, with no detective.

Bleach Bypass can drain the silver. It is a process, not the whole civic design.

How it works

Two common modes: dirty handheld 35mm with available mixed light and lens dirt (civic collapse), or monumental wides with haze, fog, and controlled orange or grey (state scale). Keep surfaces used: stains, signage, rank.

Avoid heroic rims unless the regime would light itself that way. Prompt civic scale gone cold, haze, signage, and rank, a future that already feels used.

When to use it

Use it when the system, not a single villain, has to be visible in the streets. Do not use it as generic grey sci-fi, or as neon crime with no civic rank.

Compared with similar shots

Dystopian is used civic future. Tech Noir is noir crime inside a machine night.

Bleach Bypass is a desaturated silver process. Blockbuster Gloss polishes adventure.

If the city is wet, neon, and investigative, check whether you actually want tech noir. If the sky is clean and rim-lit, you have left dystopia.

Tech NoirThe future is wet and guilty.

Bleach BypassWar, crime, or a world without mercy.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

Children of Men (handheld civic dirt, 35mm, long-take streets, a used near-future). Blade Runner 2049 (monumental fog, orange, rank, and scale).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Do not add a clean heroic rim or a detective fedora unless the story has one.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Tech Noir or Blockbuster Gloss: neon rain investigation, or a poster-clean future. The tell is a hard noir cheek with no civic rank, or a rim-lit sky.

Fix: dirty the surfaces, add signage and haze, and decide handheld-civic versus monumental-fog.

Questions

What is Dystopian in film?

A look in which civic scale, used surfaces, haze, signage, and rank make the system the antagonist. The future already looks worn. Daylight bureaucracy counts as much as night rain.

Dystopian vs Tech Noir

Tech noir is crime grammar plus future screens at night. Dystopian is the used state: queues, towers, pollution, rank, often in day. Overlap exists. They are not the same lighting plot.

When should I use Dystopian?

When the system must be visible as the threat. Skip it for silver 1940s crime, for pastel vaporwave, for glossy adventure, or for a neon detective story with no civic rank.

entries.title: Magical Realism
entries.text:
Magical Realism

Magical realism cinematography treats an extraordinary event as ordinary inside a recognizable world: the same window light, the same 35mm coverage, with one impossible fact staged as if it were weather. The camera does not gawk, add a rim, or warp the lens.

Create this Magical Realism

Narrative function

A girl sees a monster and the exposure does not change. Snow falls in a kitchen and the practicals stay kitchen practicals.

Wonder is not a lighting cue. If you add shafts, dutch angles, and a choir of haze, you have left the contract.

It is not Dreamcore (liminal rooms, unresolved memory). It is not Altered State (perception smear).

It is not blockbuster spectacle. The world stays real.

One fact does not.

How it works

Motivated naturalistic light: window, overcast, a household bulb. 35mm or 50mm, eye level, coverage as if nothing were impossible.

Play the miracle in the same size you would play a kettle. Do not under-light, dutch, or add volumetric spectacle for the impossible beat.

Prompt ordinary light, one impossible fact treated as weather.

When to use it

Use it when a miracle must not become a set-piece. Do not use it for a trip sequence, a liminal corridor, or an effects showcase.

Compared with similar shots

Magical Realism keeps ordinary light and one impossible fact. Dreamcore empties and softens the room.

Altered State warps perception. Southern Gothic can host strange events but its optical problem is heat and decay, not a calmly covered miracle.

If the camera gawks, it is spectacle, not this look.

DreamcoreNostalgia with the safety removed.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

Neo-NoirNoir after color was invented.

In film

The Spirit of the Beehive (honeyed natural light, a child's encounter played as afternoon). Beasts of the Southern Wild (aural and visual wonders inside humid daylight realism).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

The usual wrong cousin is Dreamcore, Altered State, or gloss: a liminal hall, a smear, or a volumetric miracle. The tell is a lighting change at the impossible beat.

Fix: keep the same key, the same lens height, and stage the impossibility as weather.

Questions

What is Magical Realism in film?

A look that covers extraordinary events with ordinary, motivated light and realist blocking. The camera does not change grammar for the miracle. The world stays recognizable. One fact does not.

Magical Realism vs Dreamcore

Dreamcore is an unresolved liminal interior with childhood light gone wrong. Magical realism is a real town or house with one impossible fact played like weather. Different rooms, different contracts.

When should I use Magical Realism?

When a miracle must not become spectacle. Skip it for trip warps, for empty memory halls, for cosmic scale, or for a lighting cue that announces wonder.

entries.title: Maximalism
entries.text:
Maximalism

Maximalist cinematography uses density as the point: too much color, too much pattern, ornament in every zone, and lighting that keeps the clutter readable rather than hiding it. Restraint would be a lie, so the frame is packed on purpose.

Create this Maximalism

Narrative function

Wallpaper fights the costume. A pastry fights the uniform.

Pink fights purple. The eye has no rest unless a centered axis organizes the noise (a hotel lobby) or a smash of hue refuses rest (a dance hall).

Speed and scale can join the density, but the optical fact is abundance. It is not Giallo.

Giallo stains relatively chic space with a weaponized primary. Maximalism fills the space with pattern for its own sake.

Hyper-Saturation is a grade. You can saturate a empty desert and still not be maximalist.

How it works

Short to moderate lenses (24mm to 40mm) to pack furniture and pattern. Multiple colored practicals.

High chroma, high detail, often symmetry or a center line so the density composes. Keep enough stop that wallpaper does not melt into bokeh unless a close-up needs it.

Prompt too much color, too much pattern, density as the point.

When to use it

Use it when a world is ornamental, theatrical, or stuffed, and a sparse frame would deny that world. Do not use it as a loud grade on an empty room, or as giallo threat with one gel.

Compared with similar shots

Maximalism is packed production design plus chroma. Giallo is fashion-threat primaries.

Hyper-Saturation is the grade only. Blockbuster Gloss can be relatively clean and expensive.

Arthouse empties. If you can count three competing patterns and they are all in focus, you are in maximalism.

GialloHorror that is also fashion.

Hyper-SaturationFeeling is louder than fact.

Film NoirCrime, guilt, and streetlamps.

In film

The Grand Budapest Hotel (centered density, uniforms, pastry, wallpaper as architecture). Moulin Rouge!

(theatrical color, patterned interiors, speed as ornament). Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Maximalist frame of [Subject], too much color, too much pattern, multiple practicals, density as the point, 24mm to 40mm so the clutter stays readable. Name the wallpaper and the costume clash.

Do not empty the room.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Giallo or Hyper-Saturation: one violent gel, or a loud grade on bare walls. The tell is empty negative space and a single hue.

Fix: fill every zone with pattern, keep it sharp, and let several colors compete.

Questions

What is Maximalism in film?

A dense look: ornament, pattern, and chroma packed into every zone, with light that keeps the clutter readable. Abundance is the optical fact, not a side effect.

Maximalism vs Giallo

Giallo uses primaries as threat inside often chic, relatively sparse interiors. Maximalism fills the interior with pattern for pleasure or theatrical excess. Both can be saturated. Only one is a murder-fashion plot.

When should I use Maximalism?

When restraint would lie about the world: a hotel, a stage, a stuffed apartment. Skip it for empty arthouse air, for noir silver, or for a single gelled hallway.

entries.title: Photography
entries.text:
Photography

Photographic cinematography treats the movie as a print: a single decisive frame, posed or found light, often Centered Composition or Tableau blocking, with the camera pretending it could hang on a wall. Motion is allowed, but the still is the law.

Create this Photography

Narrative function

Hold. This is the picture.

A candlelit room is arranged like a painting. A river still is exposed for the sky.

People occupy the frame as if a shutter, not a scene, were about to close. It is close to Arthouse patience but not the same.

Arthouse may be empty, slightly ugly, and long. Photography wants the print: a chosen moment, shaped light, a composition that would survive without time.

If the camera hunts, you have left the still.

How it works

Tripod. One frame.

Pose the bodies or wait for a still gesture. Light as a stills photographer would: window, candle, or a single shaped key, not a moving TV-style fill.

35mm to 85mm, sometimes a zoom used as a stills crop (as in Barry Lyndon). Prompt still-photography grammar, a single decisive frame, posed light, the movie pretending to be a print.

When to use it

Use it when the beat is a picture, not a passage. Do not use it for coverage that must cut, or for empty duration that refuses to compose.

Compared with similar shots

Photography is the print as grammar. Tableau is staged group composition.

Centered Composition is a placement rule. Arthouse may refuse the decisive moment.

Static Locked-Off is only the locked head. A photographically lit moving shot can still be this look if every frame could hang.

A locked empty hold with odd headroom is arthouse first.

In film

Barry Lyndon (candlelit stills, zoom as a painter's crop). The New World (natural light, frames that behave like exposed plates).

Grammar, not frames to copy.

The usual wrong cousin is Arthouse emptiness or a moving coverage scene: odd unused air, or a walk-and-talk. The tell is a frame that would not survive as a still, or a camera that hunts.

What is Photography in film?

A look that treats motion pictures as prints: decisive framing, posed or found stills light, often tableau or centered, with the camera behaving like a shutter rather than like coverage.
